basis: Histidine metabolism disorder explicitly defined by encephalopathy, intellectual disability and ataxia; recurrent infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency.

decisions.neurologic: primary: encephalopathy is explicit in the definition; intellectual disability and cerebellar dysfunction characterize reported cases.

basis: CD40 class-switch immunodeficiency; intrinsic neutropenia occurs in roughly half or more of patients. Secondary infections do not independently establish organ damage.

decisions.haematologic: involved: intrinsic neutropenia affects roughly half or more of patients with CD40 deficiency, exceeding the 30% threshold.

basis: Skeletal/ectodermal dysplasia with nephronophthisis; hepatic fibrosis affects ~30-50%. Dental defects (80-99%) omitted at cap in favor of severe visceral damage.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic fibrosis affects approximately 30-50% and causes substantial visceral damage; retained under the four-axis cap.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none at cap: dental defects affect 80-99%, but hepatic fibrosis is prioritized for its greater functional severity.

basis: Complex I deficiency with defining neurodevelopmental impairment (3/3); cardiac abnormalities and optic disc pallor each 1/3. Estimates derive from a small cohort.

decisions.neurologic: primary: the subtype has a defining encephalopathic phenotype, with developmental delay 3/3 and seizures, spasticity and white-matter injury 2/3.

basis: Oral/digital malformations define OFD17; tetralogy of Fallot and CNS hypomyelination each 1/1. Renal hypoplasia and hearing impairment also 1/1, omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: none at cap: renal hypoplasia occurs in 1/1, but documented cardiac and CNS abnormalities have greater demonstrated functional severity.
decisions.neurologic: involved: CNS hypomyelination and ventriculomegaly occur in 1/1; retained with severe cardiac disease under the four-axis cap.

basis: Microphthalmia defines the disease; callosal/hippocampal malformations with developmental delay and cleft lip/palate each occur in 1/1 reported patient.

decisions.neurologic: involved: structural brain malformations and developmental delay occur in 1/1; they accompany the defining microphthalmia rather than define its primary organ.

basis: Mitochondrial myopathy with immunodeficiency 2/2 and reduced CD4 cells 3/4; ptosis 3/3 and ophthalmoparesis 1/3. Possible hepatic involvement omitted at cap.

decisions.hepatic: none at cap: transaminases 3/4 may partly reflect myopathy; steatosis is reported in 1/1 assessed. Persistent ocular dysfunction has stronger evidence.
decisions.ocular: involved: persistent ptosis affects 3/3 and ophthalmoparesis 1/3, supporting direct eyelid and ocular motor dysfunction.
decisions.infectious_immune: primary: intrinsic immunodeficiency is documented in 2/2 with reduced CD4 cells in 3/4; the immunodeficiency mechanism axis belongs in primary.

basis: Renal-hepatic dysplasia and Dandy-Walker malformation define syndrome; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. Pancreatic/intestinal anomalies (30-79%) omitted at cap.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 30-79% and represents severe structural loss of lung capacity; prioritized under the cap.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none at cap: pancreatic abnormalities and intestinal malrotation occur in 30-79%; severe pulmonary hypoplasia takes the remaining slot.

basis: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with defining olfactory dysfunction, anosmia 8/8; hearing impairment 6/8. Dental defects 2/8 and occasional bone loss fall below threshold.

decisions.neurologic: primary: olfactory dysfunction is a defining component of the Kallmann phenotype and anosmia is documented in 8/8 patients.

basis: Retinal/optic degeneration, progressive glomerulopathy and cerebellar impairment define the syndrome. Hypermobility alone does not establish joint damage; scoliosis is occasional.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: joint hypermobility in 80-99% does not itself establish damage or functional loss; scoliosis occurs in only 5-29%.
